description: Patine: looks finished, feels native. A polished React Native component library for iOS, Android and the web from one codebase, with no native code: the Patine design by default, or each platform's native look with one prop. Over 100 components with a shadcn-style API: buttons, fields, selects, date, time and color pickers, dialogs, sheets, menus, toasts, tabs, lists, tables, cards, carousels, chat and more. Free outline icons in @patine-ui/icons.
rules: Install patine-ui. It has zero native code (pure JavaScript), so it works in Expo Go without a rebuild. It needs React 19 and React Native 0.78 or later (Expo SDK 53+).

With Vite, alias react-native to a small shim that re-exports react-native-web, define __DEV__ and global, and put .web.* extensions first; the full vite.config.ts and the Vitest lines are on patine.dev/docs/getting-started/installation#vite.
On native, import from feature subpaths such as 'patine-ui/date' so Metro only bundles what you use.
Names and props follow shadcn/ui: variant, size, checked + onCheckedChange, value + onValueChange, and composed parts like Card + CardHeader + CardTitle.

Every overlay (sheets, picker sheets, ActionSheet, Dialog, Modal, Popover) takes open + onOpenChange. Dialog, BottomSheet and ActionSheet also take a trigger element and defaultOpen, so a simple one needs no state.
Select, DropdownMenu and picker fields take defaultOpen. onValueChange and onOpenChange fire for user changes only, not when value or open is set programmatically.
Every platform gets the Patine design (design 'brand') by default: one finished look, with each platform's behaviour.
<PatineProvider design="native"> gives each platform its own look (iOS, Material, web); design="ios" | "material" | "web" forces one look everywhere.
A component's design prop wins over the provider's, and theme, styles and explicit props win over the design.

Fonts go in theme.typography.fonts by role (body, heading, display, numeric, mono), one family name per weight ({ regular: 'Inter_400Regular', semibold: 'Inter_600SemiBold' }); a missing role uses body, then the system font.
Patine ships no fonts: load them with Expo's useFonts and pass the names. Text takes font='numeric' for amounts (tabular figures); Heading uses 'heading'.
Text sizes are xs, sm, md, lg, xl, 2xl, 3xl, display, hero; weights regular, medium, semibold, bold. typography.lineHeights and tracking set each step; theme.density is 'comfortable' or 'compact'.

Every shadow comes from theme.shadows (none, xs, sm, md, lg, xl, as CSS box-shadow strings): override them in PatineProvider to restyle all components at once, or pick a level with a component's shadow prop.
Use Dialog for short content, AlertDialog to confirm, and Modal (full screen on phones, sizes, nests) or Drawer (side panel) for rich content.
In forms, use the field components: they own the open state and show the confirmed value.

The field components: DatePickerField, TimePickerField, DateTimePickerField, DurationPickerField, MonthPickerField, ColorPickerField, WheelPickerField, EmojiPickerField, Select, CountryPicker, LanguagePicker, PhoneField.
Gesture components (Carousel, Pager, SortableList, SwipeableRow, ImageViewer, SignaturePad) need no Reanimated or Gesture Handler.

Pro charts (LineChart, AreaChart, BarChart, ComboChart, PieChart, DonutChart, RadialChart, GaugeChart, HeatmapChart, ScatterChart, FunnelChart, RadarChart, Sparkline, StatusTracker) install with npx shadcn add @patine-pro/<type>-chart, import from @/components/patine/<type>-chart and need react-native-svg.

Pro blocks (Kanban, EventCalendar, Agenda, Gantt, Timeline, Wizard, StatsRow, PricingTable, ProductCard, ReviewList, OrderTracker, ActivityFeed, AgentActivity, AIUsageMeter) install with npx shadcn add @patine-pro/<block>, import from @/components/patine/<block> and need react-native-svg.

Pro icons: Icon with 670 names in outline, solid, duotone and color, and BrandIcon with 147 brand and social logos: npx shadcn add @patine-pro/icons or @patine-pro/brands, import from @/components/patine/icons or @/components/patine/brands (needs react-native-svg). There is no @patine-ui/pro package.
For icons, install @patine-ui/icons (MIT, needs react-native-svg) and write <Icon name="bell" />, or import { Glyph, iconBell } to ship one icon.
Find icon names with the MCP tool search_icons instead of guessing. Patine Pro's Icon takes the same names and adds variants.

Style a component's root with style and its parts with styles={{ label: …, box: … }} (styles.<slot>); there are no labelStyle/titleStyle props. A component's design and theme cascade to everything inside it.
An Icon inside a Button, Fab, tab, segment, Badge, Alert or destructive row takes that control's content color, so don't pass color there.
Translate every default word once with <PatineProvider labels={{ close: 'Fermer', pagination: { next: 'Suivant' } }}>: DEFAULT_LABELS lists the keys, and a component's own label props win.
Set text direction with dir="rtl" on PatineProvider (defaults to I18nManager on native and the page's dir on the web). useLabels() and useDirection() read them.

Build custom pressables with Touchable from patine-ui/core: role required; focus ring, disabled state, 44pt target and href included; hover={false} drops the hover tint. Theme styles go in createStyles((t) => ({ … })).

For your own components use patine-ui/core's Scroll, VirtualList, Input, Span (inherits its parent Text's style), Pressable (non-control surfaces), AnimatedView/AnimatedText instead of react-native's views and Animated.
patine-ui/core also has createAnimatedValue/createAnimatedComponent, ThemeScope to pass a theme or design down, useFocusVisible for keyboard-only rings, and IS_WEB only for DOM checks.
Chart series colours are theme.chart[i % 8] (colour-blind safe, light and dark); colours over media are theme.colors.media, onMedia, onMediaMuted, scrim and mediaTrack.
For navigation on the web, give Button, Card, ListItem, BottomTabBar/NavigationRail items or Breadcrumbs items an href (plus external for a new tab): it renders a real <a href> that crawlers follow.
An href opens the URL with Linking on iOS and Android after onPress; onPress can call event.preventDefault() to handle it in your router instead.
Prefer the root props over the shadcn parts: <Alert title="…" description="…" action={…} />, <Card title footer>, <Dialog trigger title actions={[…]}>, <Tabs items>, <Accordion items>.
Compose AlertTitle, CardHeader, DialogContent… only for layouts the props can't express. A Dialog action whose onPress calls event.preventDefault() keeps the dialog open.
